hook.line: Some requests have to be perfect: to a bank manager, a judge, a landlord who is angry. Spanish keeps its most polite rung for those moments.
hook.es: Les ruego que me disculpen por la demora.
hook.en: I ask you all to forgive me for the delay.

rule:
*Le ruego que…* ("I ask you to…") is the top rung of politeness, for strangers, officials and letters that must be perfect.

*Le* is one person (*usted*). *Les* is several.

After *que* the verb is in the subjunctive: *me envíe*, *revisen*, *me disculpen*.

For an even softer "I would ask you", use *rogaría que* and the past subjunctive: *Le rogaría que me enviara…*.

With friends you would say *¿me puedes…?* instead.
smallPrint: Teachers call *rogaría que* + imperfect subjunctive the conditional of courtesy. It softens the request by making it less direct.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *le* or *les*. You write to one manager, *usted*: ___ ruego que me responda lo antes posible. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Le ruego que me responda lo antes posible.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *envíe* or *envía*: Le ruego que me ___ la factura. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Le ruego que me envíe la factura.
yourTurn.why: After *ruego que* the verb is in the subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: I ask you all to forgive me for the delay.
yourTurn.answer: Les ruego que me disculpen por la demora.
yourTurn.why: Several people, so *les*, and *disculpen* is the subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: I kindly ask you (formal) to confirm the date.
yourTurn.answer: Le ruego que me confirme la fecha.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it softer, "I would ask you": Le ruego que me envíe el contrato.
yourTurn.answer: Le rogaría que me enviara el contrato.
yourTurn.why: *Rogaría que* goes with the past subjunctive, *enviara*.

yourTurn.prompt: Now write to several people: Le ruego que revise mi caso.
yourTurn.answer: Les ruego que revisen mi caso.

yourTurn.prompt: I ask you all to arrive on time.

pitfalls.wrong: Le ruego que me envía la factura.
pitfalls.right: Le ruego que me envíe la factura.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *ruego que* the verb needs the subjunctive, *envíe*.

pitfalls.wrong: Le ruego para que me envíe la factura.
pitfalls.right: Le ruego que me envíe la factura.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish says *ruego que* with no *para*.
Almost. You ask *to* them, so the small word is *les*, not *los*.

personal: Think of someone you would have to write to very formally. Write one request to them: *Le ruego que…*.
